form: A vertical, round brick-lined well shaft about 2.4 m across whose walls are fitted, floor-to-infinity, with the furniture of a Victorian family house turned on end: glazed cupboards, bookshelves, maps and pictures on pegs

grows_from.waking_detail: the hedge burrow plus Alice's drowsy thoughts of home, Dinah and tea-time; the shaft is the burrow's darkness furnished with the family house (LOC-family-house) schoolroom, study and pantry

mucha_design_language.item: Mucha / Art Nouveau in the shaft's fixed lining only: between the furniture bands the brick carries encircling mosaic bands of pastel-and-gold tesserae with flowing vine and poppy (sleep) motifs; the wooden pegs and shelf brackets become wrought-iron whiplash vine brackets with verdigris and traces of gilding; at intervals a round stained-glass halo roundel is set into the wall, dimly glowing from the faint daylight above; the furniture, books, maps, pictures and jars stay plain 1862 household pieces
mucha_design_language.why: The fall is listed in WR-010; the household things stay 1862 (WR-009) so the grows_from link to the family house still reads

structure.item: the entry: a short, near-level earth tunnel laced with hawthorn roots that dips suddenly into the vertical shaft
a round shaft about 2.4 m inside diameter, no visible top or bottom; the lower darkness is unlit
wall lining of soot-darkened red brick in English bond, visible between the furniture as the 'well' surface
structure.why: The source calls it a well; brick well-lining is the period well material, and it makes the domestic furniture read as wrongly placed

materials.item: mahogany and grained-deal cupboard carcasses with small-paned glazed doors and brass cup handles
materials.note: wood species inferred: upper-middle-class 1860s household furniture (world.json#frame.social_class)

materials.item: open bookshelves of stained pine loaded with cloth- and leather-bound books

details.item: cupboards and book-shelves filling the sides of the well
maps hung on wooden pegs: 1860s schoolroom wall maps of England and of Europe on rollers, and a folded map of New Zealand and Australia
details.note: map subjects inferred from Alice's fall monologue on latitude and the Antipodes (ch001-p08/p09) and the schoolroom (culture.json#CUL-027)

details.item: framed pictures on pegs: small engravings and a family silhouette in oval frames
pantry shelf with stoneware and glass jars, one labelled ORANGE MARMALADE (empty)
on one shelf, a saucer of milk set out as if for a cat
details.why: Grows from Alice's line 'I hope they'll remember her saucer of milk at tea-time' (ch001-p10), the thought she falls asleep on

interior.layout: a single vertical cylinder; furniture fixed all round the wall in stacked bands (cupboards, bookshelves, map-and-picture pegs, pantry shelf) repeating downward; the entry tunnel joins at the top
openings: entry tunnel mouth at the top of the shaft, faint daylight far above
no other openings; the bottom is unseen darkness until the landing (SCN-shaft-landing-passage)
interior.ceiling_note: no ceiling; 6.0 m is the height of the repeating rig wall section
interior.furniture_tone: the family house's schoolroom, study and pantry: respectable, slightly worn mid-Victorian mahogany and pine

scale_notes.rule: True scale (Alice 135 cm): every shelf must be within her arm's reach as she passes, since she takes down a jar and puts it back in a cupboard. Built as a vertical rig set: the furniture wall section (about 6 m tall) travels past a wire-rigged Alice rather than Alice falling past a static set; repeat the section in dressing variants so the fall reads endless.

negative: no water at the bottom, no windlass, no bucket, no rope
no CG infinite tunnel, no floating objects without fixings, no glowing or magic light
no rock cave, no mine timbering, no ladders
no furniture, books, maps or jars later than 1862 (Art Nouveau only in the mosaic bands, iron brackets and glass roundels of the lining)
no flat poster illustration, outline graphics or matte-painting finish; built rig set
no modern printed labels or plastic jars
no skeletons, bats or creatures on the shelves
prompt_ready_en: a deep round well shaft lined with soot-dark red brick banded with pastel-and-gold Art Nouveau mosaic of flowing vines and poppies in the style of Mucha, small round stained-glass roundels set in the wall, its walls fitted with Victorian glazed mahogany cupboards, bookshelves full of old books, schoolroom maps and small framed pictures hung on verdigris wrought-iron whiplash brackets, a pantry shelf with stoneware jars and one glass jar labelled ORANGE MARMALADE, darkness below, photographed live-action set
